cards.text: Job, a man who lost his children, his wealth and his health (Job 1:13-19; 2:7), has been getting question after question from the LORD. He just put his hand over his mouth and said he has nothing to add (Job 40:4-5). Then the LORD answers Job out of the whirlwind.

cards.question: Job's gone quiet, so the LORD tells him he can stop answering now.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me." Friend, "brace yourself" has never ONCE been followed by "here, have a cookie."

cards.question: The LORD asks Job if he would really annul His justice. Would Job condemn God to ___ himself?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like His?" Friend, my arms are a MUSTACHE, and the loudest voice in my old kitchen was Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids.
Then the LORD hands Job a challenge: clothe yourself with honor and glory, and unleash the fury of your wrath. That's like getting handed the keys to the whole bakery and told, okay, YOU run it.

cards.question: In the LORD's challenge, what is Job told to do to every proud man?

answers.text: Look on him and bring him low
Pray for him and let him go
Warn him and give him time

cards.question: Humble the proud, trample the wicked, bury them in the dust. If Job could pull all that off, what does the LORD say He would confess?

answers.text: That Job's own right hand can save him
That Job was right all along
That Job should rule the nations

cards.text: Then the LORD points Job to a creature: "Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you." Friend, that's like going to meet the new coworker who started the same day as you, and he's the size of the BUILDING.

cards.question: The LORD says Behemoth feeds on ___ like an ox.

cards.text: His tail sways like a cedar, his bones are tubes of bronze, and his limbs are rods of iron. All that muscle, friend, and he runs on GRASS.

cards.question: The LORD calls Behemoth the foremost of His works. Who is the only one who can draw the sword against him?
The beasts of the field run and hide when Behemoth is nearby.

cards.text: So where does a creature this big hang out? Under the lotus plants, hidden in the reeds of the marsh, like me napping in the shade after a big batch.
But what if the river rages? What if the Jordan surges right up to his mouth?

cards.question: Even when the river rages, Behemoth stays unafraid and secure.
The LORD finishes with Behemoth on one last question. What does it ask?

cards.text: Pierce his nose with a snare while he WATCHES you? Friend, I spent a whole morning chasing one sprinkle under the oven and never caught it.
Then the LORD turns to another creature, Leviathan: "Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?"

cards.question: The LORD keeps the questions coming about Leviathan. What are they all asking Job?

answers.text: Whether Job could tame and control him
Whether Job has ever seen him up close
Whether Job knows where he lives

cards.text: "Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?" Friend, I'm stuck on a GOLD BASE, so if I put Leviathan on a leash, he's walking ME.

cards.question: The LORD says if Job lays a hand on Leviathan, he'll remember the ___ and never repeat it.

cards.text: Any hope of overcoming him is false, and just the sight of him is overwhelming. No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan.

cards.question: Nobody dares stir up Leviathan. What question does the LORD ask right after that?

answers.text: Who is able to stand against Me
Who is brave enough to hunt him
Who will warn the people of the sea

cards.question: The LORD says He has to repay people for what they've given Him.

cards.text: The LORD says, "Everything under heaven is Mine." Friend, I can't even hand Him a cookie that didn't come out of an oven He gave me.
Then the LORD says He can't keep silent about Leviathan's limbs, his power and graceful form. His rows of scales are his pride.

cards.question: What does the LORD say about the space between Leviathan's scales?

answers.text: So tight no air can pass between them
Loose enough for water to slip through
Spread apart like feathers on a wing

cards.text: And then it gets WILD. His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.

cards.question: Fire and smoke come out of Leviathan, with flames from his mouth and smoke from his nostrils.

cards.text: His breath sets coals ablaze. Friend, I've spent YEARS preheating ovens, and this guy does it just by BREATHING.
Strength resides in his neck, his chest is as hard as a rock, and when he rises up, even the mighty are terrified.

cards.question: An arrow can make Leviathan flee.

cards.text: He regards iron as straw, and he LAUGHS at the sound of the lance. Friend, somebody drops one cookie tray near me and I jump a foot in the air, gold base and all.

cards.question: Leviathan leaves a glistening wake, and one would think the deep had white hair. How does the LORD sum him up?

answers.text: Nothing on earth is his equal
He is the oldest of all creatures
He is afraid only of the deep

cards.question: The LORD's last line about Leviathan: he is king over all the ___.

cards.text: Then Job replies to the LORD. Friend, after hearing about a creature whose breath sets coals ablaze, I'd need a minute.

cards.question: Job starts with what he now knows. What is it?

answers.text: That God can do all things

cards.question: Job admits he spoke about things he did not understand, things too wonderful for him to know.

cards.text: Then Job quotes the LORD back: "I will question you, and you shall inform Me." That line again, from the start of this whole speech.

cards.question: Job tells the LORD how the way he knows God has changed. What's different between before and now?

answers.text: Before he'd heard of God but now he's seen Him
Before he'd doubted God but now he trusts Him
Before he'd feared God but now he loves Him

cards.question: Job's last words here: therefore he despises himself, and he ___ in dust and ashes.

cards.text: And that's where we leave Job for now, in dust and ashes. Hang tight, friend, because this story's got one more page.
